title: Deeper/broader DXF inspector and template-preservation route audit
mode: Primary-source web research and plan refinement; no peer execution
baselineQualification: The shared worktree was broadly dirty at review start. Plan and local status observations refer to the shared worktree, not a clean checkout at baselineCommit.
scope: Screen newly surfaced DXF-only routes for implementation evidence relevant to source inspection, 2D consumers, and template-scoped byte preservation.
Separate parser projection, renderer behavior, raw preservation, semantic rewrite, and whole-document support claims.
Add only optional, implementation-ready comparator guidance where it refines the existing plan without promoting support claims.

method.kind: Current primary-source repository and README review, cross-checked against the local parity plan

sources.revision: Mutable main/repository pages reviewed 2026-10-18; no immutable commit selected
sources.observed: The README describes text and supported-binary DXF inspection, source-tree and handle navigation, diagnostics, structural comparison, rendering, editing, and DXF export. It explicitly disclaims DWG I/O, an ACIS kernel, arbitrary DXF object-graph import, and full AutoCAD fidelity. This pass did not inspect parser call sites, source/package boundaries, or code lineage with the author's other CAD projects.

sources.revision: Mutable main/repository pages reviewed 2026-10-18; repository page showed three commits and no listed release
sources.observed: The README claims AC1032 DXF read/write for template workflows, byte-for-byte preservation of selected untouched CLASSES/TABLES/BLOCKS sections, TEXT/MTEXT replacement, IMAGE/IMAGEDEF insertion, and generic unknown entity/object wrappers. The source, actual preserved byte ranges, regression inputs, and outputs were not audited or executed.

sources.revision: Mutable master/repository pages reviewed 2026-10-18; no immutable commit selected
sources.observed: The README describes a JavaScript DXF-to-object parser covering header, common 2D entities, tables, blocks/inserts, VPORT, text/some MTEXT, and some XData; it explicitly lists 3DSOLID and less-common entities/objects as unsupported. This documents a projection boundary, not whole-document retention.

assessment.planImpact: Adds two optional DXF comparator roles: browser/source-tree inspection of exposed text and supported-binary content, and template-scoped raw-section preservation. It tightens the evidence boundary between projection, visualization, selective byte preservation, semantic rewrite, and whole-document completeness. It does not create a required peer, local finding, implementation task, fixture, dependency, test cadence, or support claim.

implementationReadyChecks: Select an exact unresolved local behavior before choosing either comparator; pin immutable source, runtime/toolchain, input hash, DXF version/encoding, and operation.
For inspector routes, compare exact exposed group-code values and handles separately from diagnostics, typed projection, rendering, and omitted/unexposed records.

For template-preservation routes, partition source into untouched and edited regions; byte-compare only the regions the implementation explicitly promises to preserve, then independently validate regenerated content and references.
Use an already-admitted DXF or a locally generated scratch control; add no externally sourced DWG/DXF fixture and do not add the peer as a routine dependency.
Keep fast local selector, strict owning target, and owning CTest as the per-slice lane; peer and native checks remain at existing composed checkpoints.

workingTree.scope: Updated the plan and added this research receipt only; unrelated dirty worktree changes were preserved.
